  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""Batch verification and cross-site aggregation of final fork decision
2	aggregate chain fork decisions -- private implementation module.
3	
4	This module is the extracted home of the
5	:mod:`offline_coordination.replication` layer in which the single final
6	fork decision aggregate chain fork decision ruling
7	(``verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_decision``, which binds
8	six policy digests) gets a batch re-check and a cross-site convergence
9	aggregate.  The batch verifier validates the decision list, the five
10	invariant policies, the proof site policy, the keyring and the moment in
11	full before any decision is parsed and reports each decision in input
12	order and in isolation.  The aggregate re-verifies, authenticates and
13	authorizes every decision against a new decision site policy, treats the
14	complete declaration (the common fork edge set -- empty for a fork-free
15	decision -- the stably sorted per-item conclusions, the term-by-term
16	proof digest vector and the overall status) as one site's vote, and seals
17	the threshold outcome with seven policy digest bindings.  The offline
18	aggregate review recomputes every binding from the aggregate bytes alone.
19	
20	This is an internal boundary, not a public entry point: the public
21	functions and the dedicated aggregate error are re-exported from
22	``offline_coordination.replication`` under their historical names, with
23	identical call signatures and class object identity.
24	
25	The shared responsibilities of the three entry points live in exactly one
26	component each: ``_ffdacf_validated_decision_materials`` (with
27	``_ffdac_bind_runtime`` and ``_ffdacfda_bind_decision_policy``) owns the
28	input pre-validation, ``_FFDACFDA_DIGEST_BINDINGS`` together with
29	``_ffdacfda_policy_digests``/``_ffdacfda_assert_policy_digests`` owns the
30	seven policy digest bindings, ``_ffdac_assert_payload_signature`` (raise
31	style) and ``_ffdacfd_key_entry_at`` (row style) own the signature
32	identity determination, ``_tally_pfda_rows`` with
33	``_ffdacfda_row_sort_key`` owns the deterministic site vote merging,
34	``_fac_chain_item_report`` owns the fixed-key-order batch item report,
35	``_reject_duplicate_pfda_keys`` owns the duplicate-key rejection, and
36	``_ffdac_parse_envelope``/``_prune_compact`` own the canonical encoding --
37	every one of them imported from ``offline_coordination.replication`` or
38	defined once below, never copied.

314	    keyring, moment,

316	    """Verify a batch of final fork decision aggregate chain fork

320	    keys ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the batch) and

322	    :func:`adjudicate_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_forks`

331	    duplicate id or a wrong item key set raises :class:`ValueError` (the

337	    :func:`verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_decision`

342	    passing decision is ``verified``.

358	    )

361	        ITEMS: [
362	            _verify_ffdacfd_decision_item(item, materials)
363	            for item in validated_items

370	def _aggregate_ffdacfda_one(item: dict, materials: dict) -> dict:
371	    """Re-verify, authenticate and authorize one decision in isolation.
372	
373	    The decision bytes first pass the exact final fork decision
374	    aggregate chain fork decision structural, positional-proof and
375	    six-policy binding rules, then the HMAC is checked against the
376	    current keyring, and finally the exact payload issuer and key
377	    version are authorized against the decision site policy with no
378	    fallback.  Any failure rejects just this row with one fixed reason
379	    (``invalid``, ``unauthenticated`` or ``unauthorized``) and never
380	    affects the other items.
381	    """
382	    item_id = item[ID]
383	    raw = item[_FFDACFDA_PACKET]
384	    decision_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
385	
386	    def invalid_row() -> dict:
387	        return _pfda_aggregate_row(
388	            item_id, decision_digest, None, None, None,
389	            PA_CONCLUSION_INVALID, PA_CONCLUSION_INVALID,
390	        )
391	
392	    try:
393	        payload, signature = _parse_ffdacf_decision(raw)
394	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
395	        return invalid_row()
396	
397	    site = payload[VD_ISSUER]
398	    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
399	
400	    try:
401	        _ffdacf_assert_decision_payload(payload, materials)
402	    except InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkDecisionError:
403	        return invalid_row()
404	
405	    def unauthenticated_row() -> dict:
406	        return _pfda_aggregate_row(
407	            item_id, decision_digest, site, key_version, None,
408	            PA_CONCLUSION_INVALID, PA_REASON_UNAUTHENTICATED,
409	        )
410	
411	    key_entry = _ffdacfd_key_entry_at(
412	        materials["keyring"], site, key_version, materials["moment"]
413	    )
414	    if key_entry is None or not hmac.compare_digest(
415	        _ffdac_payload_signature(key_entry, payload), signature
416	    ):
417	        return unauthenticated_row()
418	
419	    # The exact-issuer HMAC established the site/version identity, so an
420	    # authorized-policy miss may carry that identity.
421	    allowed_versions = materials["decision_site_policy"][ADJ_SITES].get(site)
422	    if allowed_versions is None or key_version not in allowed_versions:
423	        return _pfda_aggregate_row(
424	            item_id, decision_digest, site, key_version, None,
425	            PA_CONCLUSION_INVALID, PA_REASON_UNAUTHORIZED,
426	        )
427	
428	    return _pfda_aggregate_row(
429	        item_id, decision_digest, site, key_version,
430	        _pfda_declaration(payload), PA_CONCLUSION_VALID, None,
431	    )

434	def aggregate_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_decisions(

436	    signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy, proof_site_policy,

439	    """Aggregate multi-site final fork decision aggregate chain fork

442	    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item contains exactly a unique,
443	    non-empty str ``id`` and ``decision`` bytes produced by
444	    :func:`adjudicate_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_forks`; the
445	    whole batch structure is validated before any decision is parsed.
446	    ``prune_policy`` is the shared invariant original pruning policy,
447	    ``authorization_policy`` the invariant site authorization policy,
448	    ``site_policy`` the invariant fork-proof signer site policy,
449	    ``signer_site_policy`` the invariant adjudication signer site
450	    policy, ``adjudication_site_policy`` the invariant issuing
451	    adjudication site policy and ``proof_site_policy`` the proof signer
452	    site policy the decisions were issued against;
453	    ``decision_site_policy`` carries exactly ``sites`` (a non-empty
454	    mapping of each decision site authorized to hand over decisions to
455	    its non-empty set of allowed positive key versions) and
456	    ``threshold`` (a positive integer no greater than the site count).
457	    ``keyring`` follows the existing rules, ``moment`` is the current
458	    time and ``issuer``/``version`` name the aggregate signing identity
459	    and key version.  No file is read or written and no input is
460	    modified.
461	
462	    Every decision is first re-verified on its own through the exact
463	    :func:`verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_decision`
464	    rules -- canonical structure, all six decision policy digest
465	    bindings, the term-by-term proof digest bindings and a full
466	    re-tally of the bound per-proof rows -- then authenticated against
467	    the current keyring by its exact payload issuer and key version,
468	    and finally authorized precisely against ``decision_site_policy``
469	    with no fallback: a structurally illegal decision or one with a
470	    broken binding is recorded ``invalid`` with reason ``invalid`` (and
471	    carries no identity), unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired
472	    credentials or a wrong signature ``unauthenticated``, and an
473	    authenticated but unauthorized site or key version
474	    ``unauthorized``, each rejecting only that item while the others
475	    continue.  A valid decision counts as the issuing site's complete
476	    declaration: the common fork edge set (empty for a fork-free
477	    decision), the per-item conclusions (stably sorted by site then id,
478	    each entry carrying its conclusion, proof digest, authenticated
479	    fork edges or null, id, reason and site), the term-by-term proof
480	    digest vector and the overall status.  For one site, declarations
481	    fully identical on every field count once and exact repeats are
482	    ``duplicate``; any field difference is a ``contradiction``.
483	    Distinct sites must agree on that same complete declaration -- any
484	    difference makes the aggregate ``conflicted``, the common
485	    declaration is bound null and no majority can outvote the
486	    disagreement.  One unique declaration backed by at least the
487	    threshold of distinct sites is ``accepted``; short of the
488	    threshold it stays ``insufficient`` but still carries that common
489	    declaration; with no valid vote the declaration is null.

492	    recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte,

495	    input order), ``issuer``, ``items`` (the rows stably sorted by
496	    issuer then id, each carrying ``conclusion``, the decision

498	    authenticated ``declaration`` or null), ``keyVersion``,
499	    ``prunePolicyDigest``, ``authorizationPolicyDigest``,
500	    ``sitePolicyDigest``, ``signerSitePolicyDigest``,
501	    ``adjudicationSitePolicyDigest``, ``proofSitePolicyDigest``,
502	    ``decisionSitePolicyDigest``, ``declaration`` (the one common
503	    complete declaration, or null), ``status`` and ``version`` (the

505	    lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes
506	    under the exact issuer/version key.
507	
508	    A parameter, container or public field type fault raises
509	    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); an
510	    empty list, an empty or duplicate id or an illegal policy,
511	    threshold, moment, site, version or issuer raises
512	    :class:`ValueError`; unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired

514	    """
515	    validated_items = _validated_cfd_decision_items(items)
516	    materials = _ffdacf_validated_decision_materials(

518	        signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy, proof_site_policy,
519	    )
520	    _ffdacfda_bind_decision_policy(materials, decision_site_policy)
521	    _ffdac_bind_runtime(materials, keyring, moment)

523	
524	    rows = [
525	        _aggregate_ffdacfda_one(item, materials)
526	        for item in validated_items
527	    ]
528	    input_digests = [row[CP_DIGEST] for row in rows]
529	    status, common_declaration = _tally_pfda_rows(
530	        rows, materials["decision_site_policy"][ADJ_THRESHOLD]
531	    )
532	    rows.sort(key=_ffdacfda_row_sort_key)
533	
534	    signing_entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
535	        materials["keyring"], issuer, version, materials["moment"]
536	    )
537	    payload = {
538	        _FACFDA_INPUTS: input_digests,
539	        VD_ISSUER: issuer,
540	        ITEMS: rows,
541	        KEY_VERSION: version,
542	        **_ffdacfda_policy_digests(materials),
543	        _FACFDA_DECLARATION: common_declaration,
544	        STATUS: status,
545	        VERSION:
546	            FINAL_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_VERSION,
547	    }
548	    signature = _ffdac_payload_signature(signing_entry, payload)
549	    return _prune_compact({TICKET_PAYLOAD: payload, SIGNATURE: signature})

552	def _parse_ffdacfda(raw: object) -> tuple[dict, str]:
553	    """Validate final fork decision aggregate chain fork decision
554	    aggregate bytes structurally.
555	
556	    A non-bytes argument or a public field of the wrong JSON type raises
557	    :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int); every
558	    encoding, key-set, version, digest, ordering, row-shape or
559	    declaration-shape fault raises
560	    :class:`InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError`.
561	    The seven policy digests, the tally and the credential bindings are
562	    checked by
563	    :func:`verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_decision_aggregate`.
564	    A counted declaration may carry the empty common fork edge set (a
565	    fork-free decision).
566	    """
567	    data, payload, signature = _ffdac_parse_envelope(
568	        raw, noun="aggregate packet", invalid=_ffdacfda_invalid,
569	        reject_duplicate=_reject_duplicate_ffdacfda_keys,
570	        payload_keys=_FFDACFDA_PAYLOAD_KEYS,
571	        payload_keys_error=(
572	            "aggregate packet payload must contain exactly the keys "
573	            "'inputs', 'issuer', 'items', 'keyVersion', "
574	            "'prunePolicyDigest', 'authorizationPolicyDigest', "
575	            "'sitePolicyDigest', 'signerSitePolicyDigest', "
576	            "'adjudicationSitePolicyDigest', 'proofSitePolicyDigest', "
577	            "'decisionSitePolicyDigest', 'declaration', 'status' and "
578	            "'version'"
579	        ),
580	        invalid_noun="aggregate packet",
581	    )
582	
583	    issuer = payload[VD_ISSUER]
584	    if not isinstance(issuer, str):
585	        raise TypeError("aggregate payload issuer must be a str")
586	    if issuer == "":
587	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
588	            "aggregate payload issuer must be a non-empty str"
589	        )
590	    key_version = payload[KEY_VERSION]
591	    if isinstance(key_version, bool) or not isinstance(key_version, int):
592	        raise TypeError("aggregate payload keyVersion must be an int")
593	    if key_version <= 0:
594	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
595	            "aggregate payload keyVersion must be positive"
596	        )
597	    for field in _FFDACFDA_DIGEST_FIELDS:
598	        digest = payload[field]
599	        if not isinstance(digest, str):
600	            raise TypeError(f"aggregate payload {field} must be a str")
601	        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
602	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
603	                f"aggregate payload {field} must be 64 lowercase hex "
604	                "characters"
605	            )
606	    status = payload[STATUS]
607	    if not isinstance(status, str):
608	        raise TypeError("aggregate status must be a str")
609	    if status not in _PA_STATUSES:
610	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid("aggregate status is not a known status")
611	    aggregate_version = payload[VERSION]
612	    if isinstance(aggregate_version, bool) or not isinstance(
613	        aggregate_version, int
614	    ):
615	        raise TypeError("aggregate payload version must be an int")
616	    if aggregate_version != (
617	        FINAL_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_VERSION
618	    ):
619	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
620	            "aggregate payload version must be the integer 1"
621	        )
622	
623	    inputs = payload[_FACFDA_INPUTS]
624	    if not isinstance(inputs, list):
625	        raise TypeError("aggregate inputs must be a list")
626	    if not inputs:
627	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid("aggregate inputs must be a non-empty list")
628	    for position, digest in enumerate(inputs):
629	        if not isinstance(digest, str):
630	            raise TypeError(f"aggregate input {position} digest must be a str")
631	        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
632	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
633	                f"aggregate input {position} digest must be 64 lowercase "
634	                "hex characters"
635	            )
636	
637	    rows = payload[ITEMS]
638	    if not isinstance(rows, list):
639	        raise TypeError("aggregate items must be a list")
640	    if not rows:
641	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid("aggregate items must be a non-empty list")
642	    if len(rows) != len(inputs):
643	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
644	            "the items must cover every input and vice versa"
645	        )
646	    seen_row_ids: set[str] = set()
647	    parsed_rows: list[dict] = []
648	    for position, row in enumerate(rows):
649	        where = f"aggregate item {position}"
650	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
651	            raise TypeError(f"{where} must be an object")
652	        if set(row.keys()) != _PFDA_ROW_KEYS:
653	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
654	                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'conclusion', "
655	                "'digest', 'id', 'issuer', 'keyVersion', 'reason' and "
656	                "'declaration'"
657	            )
658	        row_id = row[ID]
659	        if not isinstance(row_id, str):
660	            raise TypeError(f"{where} id must be a str")
661	        if row_id == "":
662	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(f"{where} id must be non-empty")
663	        if row_id in seen_row_ids:
664	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(f"{where} repeats an id")

666	        digest = row[CP_DIGEST]
667	        if not isinstance(digest, str):
668	            raise TypeError(f"{where} digest must be a str")
669	        if not _prune_is_digest(digest):
670	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
671	                f"{where} digest must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
672	            )
673	        row_site = row[VD_ISSUER]
674	        if row_site is not None and not isinstance(row_site, str):
675	            raise TypeError(f"{where} issuer must be a str or null")
676	        if row_site == "":
677	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(f"{where} issuer must be non-empty")
678	        row_key_version = row[KEY_VERSION]
679	        if isinstance(row_key_version, bool) or not isinstance(
680	            row_key_version, int
681	        ):
682	            if row_key_version is not None:
683	                raise TypeError(f"{where} keyVersion must be an int or null")
684	        elif row_key_version <= 0:
685	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(f"{where} keyVersion must be positive")
686	        if (row_site is None) != (row_key_version is None):
687	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
688	                f"{where} issuer and keyVersion must be null together"
689	            )
690	        conclusion = row[ADJ_CONCLUSION]
691	        if not isinstance(conclusion, str):
692	            raise TypeError(f"{where} conclusion must be a str")
693	        reason = row[ADJ_REASON]
694	        if conclusion == PA_CONCLUSION_VALID:
695	            if reason is not None:
696	                raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
697	                    f"{where} reason must be null for a valid row"
698	                )
699	        elif conclusion == PA_CONCLUSION_INVALID:
700	            if reason not in _PFDA_INVALID_REASONS:
701	                raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
702	                    f"{where} reason must be one of 'invalid', "
703	                    "'unauthenticated' or 'unauthorized'"
704	                )
705	        elif conclusion in (
706	            PA_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE, PA_CONCLUSION_CONTRADICTION
707	        ):
708	            expected = (
709	                REASON_DUPLICATE
710	                if conclusion == PA_CONCLUSION_DUPLICATE
711	                else REASON_CONTRADICTION
712	            )
713	            if reason != expected:
714	                raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
715	                    f"{where} reason must match its conclusion"
716	                )
717	        else:
718	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(f"{where} conclusion is not known")
719	        identity_present = reason != PA_CONCLUSION_INVALID
720	        if identity_present:
721	            if row_site is None:
722	                raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
723	                    f"{where} an authenticated or authorized row must carry "
724	                    "its issuer"
725	                )
726	        elif row_site is not None:
727	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
728	                f"{where} an invalid row must carry no issuer"
729	            )
730	        raw_declaration = row[_FACFDA_DECLARATION]
731	        if conclusion == PA_CONCLUSION_INVALID:
732	            if raw_declaration is not None:
733	                raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
734	                    f"{where} an invalid row must carry no declaration"
735	                )
736	            parsed_declaration = None
737	        else:
738	            parsed_declaration = _validated_pfda_declaration(
739	                raw_declaration, f"{where} declaration",
740	                invalid=_ffdacfda_invalid, positional_proofs=True,
741	                allow_empty_edges=True,
742	            )
743	            if parsed_declaration is None:
744	                raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
745	                    f"{where} a counted row must carry its declaration"
746	                )
747	        parsed_rows.append({
748	            ADJ_CONCLUSION: conclusion,
749	            CP_DIGEST: digest,
750	            ID: row_id,
751	            VD_ISSUER: row_site,
752	            KEY_VERSION: row_key_version,
753	            ADJ_REASON: reason,
754	            _FACFDA_DECLARATION: parsed_declaration,
755	        })
756	
757	    common_declaration = _validated_pfda_declaration(
758	        payload[_FACFDA_DECLARATION], "aggregate declaration",
759	        invalid=_ffdacfda_invalid, positional_proofs=True,
760	        allow_empty_edges=True,
761	    )
762	
763	    normalized_payload = {
764	        _FACFDA_INPUTS: list(inputs),
765	        VD_ISSUER: issuer,
766	        ITEMS: parsed_rows,
767	        KEY_VERSION: key_version,
768	        _FACFDA_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST: payload[_FACFDA_PRUNE_POLICY_DIGEST],
769	        _FACFDA_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY_DIGEST: payload[
770	            _FACFDA_AUTHORIZATION_POLICY_DIGEST
771	        ],
772	        _FACFDA_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: payload[_FACFDA_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST],
773	        _FACFDA_SIGNER_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: payload[
774	            _FACFDA_SIGNER_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST
775	        ],
776	        _FACFDA_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: payload[
777	            _FACFDA_ADJUDICATION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST
778	        ],
779	        _FFDACFDA_PROOF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: payload[
780	            _FFDACFDA_PROOF_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST
781	        ],
782	        _FFDACFDA_DECISION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST: payload[
783	            _FFDACFDA_DECISION_SITE_POLICY_DIGEST
784	        ],
785	        _FACFDA_DECLARATION: common_declaration,
786	        STATUS: status,
787	        VERSION:
788	            FINAL_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_CHAIN_FORK_DECISION_AGGREGATE_VERSION,
789	    }
790	    if _prune_compact({TICKET_PAYLOAD: normalized_payload,
791	                       SIGNATURE: signature}) != raw:
792	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
793	            "aggregate packet encoding is not the canonical compact form"
794	        )
795	    return normalized_payload, signature

804	    digest vector are re-tallied through the exact final fork decision
805	    aggregate chain fork decision rules against the proof site policy
806	    threshold, so a reordered entry, a reordered proof summary, a wrong
807	    duplicate or contradiction marking, a tampered common set or a
808	    mis-stated status cannot hide inside a counted declaration.  Any
809	    mismatch raises
810	    :class:`InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError`.
811	    """
812	    synthetic_payload = {
813	        PAFD_COMMON: declaration[PAFD_COMMON],
814	        ITEMS: [
815	            {
816	                ADJ_CONCLUSION: entry[ADJ_CONCLUSION],
817	                PAFD_EDGES: entry[PAFD_EDGES],
818	                ID: entry[ID],
819	                KEY_VERSION: None,
820	                PAFD_FORK_PROOF_DIGEST: entry[CP_DIGEST],
821	                ADJ_REASON: entry[ADJ_REASON],
822	                VD_ISSUER: entry[VD_ISSUER],
823	            }
824	            for entry in declaration[PFDA_CONCLUSIONS]
825	        ],
826	        PAFD_PROOFS: declaration[PFDA_PROOFS],
827	        STATUS: declaration[STATUS],
828	    }
829	    try:
830	        _reconcile_pafd(
831	            synthetic_payload, fork_threshold,
832	            invalid=_ffdacf_decision_invalid, positional_proofs=True,
833	        )
834	    except InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkDecisionError as exc:
835	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid(f"{where}: {exc}") from exc

838	def _reconcile_ffdacfda_aggregate(
839	    payload: dict, fork_threshold: int, decision_threshold: int
840	) -> None:
841	    """Re-derive every binding of a parsed decision aggregate payload.
842	
843	    Re-tallies the per-decision rows the signature covers -- the
844	    original-order input digest bindings, row ordering, same-site
845	    duplicate and contradiction markings, cross-site complete
846	    declaration agreement, the threshold acceptance and the claimed
847	    common declaration and status -- and re-tallies every counted
848	    declaration against the proof site policy threshold, without seeing
849	    any decision bytes.  Any mismatch raises
850	    :class:`InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError`.
851	    """
852	    rows = payload[ITEMS]
853	    inputs = payload[_FACFDA_INPUTS]
854	
855	    expected_order = sorted(rows, key=_ffdacfda_row_sort_key)
856	    if [row[ID] for row in expected_order] != [row[ID] for row in rows]:
857	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid("items must be sorted by issuer then id")
858	    if sorted(row[CP_DIGEST] for row in rows) != sorted(inputs):
859	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
860	            "the bound input digests must equal the per-item digests"
861	        )
862	
863	    # Deep-copy the parsed rows before the tally mutates their
864	    # conclusion/reason markings; the signed payload itself is compared
865	    # through freshly derived structures only.
866	    working_rows = copy.deepcopy(rows)
867	    derived_status, derived_declaration = _tally_pfda_rows(
868	        working_rows, decision_threshold
869	    )
870	
871	    for expected_row, bound_row in zip(working_rows, rows):
872	        if expected_row[ADJ_CONCLUSION] != bound_row[ADJ_CONCLUSION]:
873	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
874	                f"item {bound_row[ID]!r} has the wrong conclusion"
875	            )
876	        if expected_row[ADJ_REASON] != bound_row[ADJ_REASON]:
877	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
878	                f"item {bound_row[ID]!r} has the wrong reason"
879	            )
880	
881	    if payload[STATUS] != derived_status:
882	        raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
883	            "the bound status does not match the tallied items"
884	        )
885	    bound_declaration = payload[_FACFDA_DECLARATION]
886	    if derived_declaration is None:
887	        if bound_declaration is not None:
888	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
889	                "the common declaration must be null when no unique "
890	                "conflict-free declaration was tallied"
891	            )
892	    else:
893	        if bound_declaration is None:
894	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
895	                "an aggregate over one unique conflict-free declaration "
896	                "must carry the common declaration"
897	            )
898	        if bound_declaration != derived_declaration:
899	            raise _ffdacfda_invalid(
900	                "the bound common declaration does not match the tallied "
901	                "decisions"
902	            )
903	
904	    for row in rows:
905	        declaration = row[_FACFDA_DECLARATION]
906	        if declaration is None:
907	            continue
908	        _reconcile_ffdacfda_declaration(
909	            declaration, fork_threshold, f"aggregate item {row[ID]!r}"
910	        )
911	    if bound_declaration is not None:
912	        _reconcile_ffdacfda_declaration(
913	            bound_declaration, fork_threshold, "aggregate declaration"
914	        )
915

917	def verify_final_fork_decision_aggregate_chain_fork_decision_aggregate(
918	    aggregate, prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy,
919	    signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy, proof_site_policy,
920	    decision_site_policy, keyring, moment,
921	):
922	    """Verify a signed final fork decision aggregate chain fork
923	    decision aggregate entirely offline.
924	
925	    Only the aggregate bytes, the seven expected policies (the original
926	    prune policy, the site authorization policy, the fork-proof signer
927	    site policy, the adjudication signer site policy, the issuing
928	    adjudication site policy, the proof site policy and the decision
929	    site policy), the current ``keyring`` and the verification
930	    ``moment`` are consulted -- no file is read or written and no
931	    argument is modified.  Verification validates the canonical
932	    encoding and every key set, recomputes all seven policy digests,
933	    and re-tallies the bound per-decision rows purely from the signed
934	    payload: the original-order input digest bindings, the issuer/id
935	    row ordering, same-site duplicate and contradiction markings,
936	    cross-site complete declaration agreement (the common fork edge
937	    set -- empty for a fork-free consensus -- the per-item conclusions,
938	    the term-by-term proof digest vector and the overall status
939	    together), the threshold outcome and the claimed common
940	    declaration, together with a full re-tally of every counted
941	    declaration against the proof site policy threshold.  It then
942	    checks the HMAC-SHA256 against the key the *current* keyring binds
943	    to the payload's exact issuer and version, usable at the
944	    verification moment, so a later revocation or expiry rejects the
945	    aggregate with no fallback.
946	
947	    On success a fresh, depth-independent result equal to the
948	    authenticated payload plus ``aggregateDigest`` (the SHA-256 of the
949	    aggregate bytes) is returned with the fixed keys
950	    ``aggregateDigest``, ``inputs``, ``issuer``, ``items``,
951	    ``keyVersion``, ``prunePolicyDigest``,
952	    ``authorizationPolicyDigest``, ``sitePolicyDigest``,
953	    ``signerSitePolicyDigest``, ``adjudicationSitePolicyDigest``,
954	    ``proofSitePolicyDigest``, ``decisionSitePolicyDigest``,
955	    ``declaration``, ``status`` and ``version`` (the integer 1) --
956	    repeated calls return equal but mutually independent objects
957	    sharing no mutable structure, and unauthenticated identities never
958	    enter a result.  A non-bytes aggregate or a field of the wrong type
959	    raises :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int);
960	    a null value, a duplicate id, a wrong key set or an illegal policy,
961	    threshold, moment or other value raises :class:`ValueError`; an
962	    illegal aggregate structure, binding or recomputation raises
963	    :class:`InvalidFinalForkDecisionAggregateChainForkDecisionAggregateError`
964	    (a :class:`ValueError` subclass, distinct from the proof, the
965	    single-decision and every other aggregate error class); unknown,
966	    revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a signature
967	    mismatch raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.
968	    """
969	    if not isinstance(aggregate, bytes):
970	        raise TypeError("aggregate packet must be bytes")
971	    materials = _ffdacf_validated_decision_materials(
972	        prune_policy, authorization_policy, site_policy,
973	        signer_site_policy, adjudication_site_policy, proof_site_policy,
974	    )
975	    _ffdacfda_bind_decision_policy(materials, decision_site_policy)
976	    _ffdac_bind_runtime(materials, keyring, moment)
977	
978	    payload, signature = _parse_ffdacfda(aggregate)
979	    _ffdacfda_assert_policy_digests(payload, materials)
980	    _reconcile_ffdacfda_aggregate(
981	        payload,
982	        materials["proof_site_policy"][ADJ_THRESHOLD],
983	        materials["decision_site_policy"][ADJ_THRESHOLD],
984	    )
985	    _ffdac_assert_payload_signature(
986	        materials["keyring"], payload[VD_ISSUER], payload[KEY_VERSION],
987	        materials["moment"], payload, signature,
988	        "final fork decision aggregate chain fork decision aggregate "
989	        "signature does not match",
990	    )
991	
992	    authenticated = copy.deepcopy(payload)
993	    return {
994	        key: (
995	            hashlib.sha256(aggregate).hexdigest()
996	            if key == _FACFDA_AGGREGATE_DIGEST
997	            else authenticated[key]
998	        )
999	        for key in _FFDACFDA_RESULT_KEYS
1000	    }
